item.title: [github_trending] MadsLorentzen/ai-job-search
item.description: MadsLorentzen/ai-job-search is an AI-powered job application framework built on Claude Code that runs locally on your machine. After forking the repo and filling in your profile, Claude evaluates job postings, tailors your CV, writes cover letters, and prepares you for interviews. It is an independent open-source project, not affiliated with Anthropic.

item.title: [juejin] Cursor 转 Codex 大半个月，聊聊我的真实感受
item.description: A Juejin post by a developer who switched from Cursor to Codex and has used it for roughly half a month. Cursor, the author says, was his first strong taste of what AI coding can do, while Codex feels less like a coding assistant and more like an autonomous super-agent, closer to the next stage of tooling. Useful for developers weighing which AI coding tool to adopt.

It is a quick scan of the day's consumer-electronics pricing, capital-market moves and tech-industry news.

item.title: [infoq] Akka 在 65 个开源项目中测试基于规格的 AI 交付
item.description: Akka ran a spec-driven AI porting workflow across 65 open source projects, spending 99.3 hours and 9.41 billion tokens in the first round; 57 of the ports improved either line count or performance. Claude worked with Akka Specify on implementation and review, with Sonnet averaging 61 minutes per port versus 120 for Opus, which used roughly 40% fewer tokens. Relevant for teams weighing AI-assisted large-scale code migration.

item.title: [v2ex] [分享创造] [开源&极重] Kokoro 探针 1.0 版发布，你没用过的博客式探针
item.description: Kokoro Probe 1.0 is an AGPL-3.0 monitoring panel built as a hub plus agent, shipping prebuilt Linux amd64/arm64 binaries and a one-line installer for Debian/Ubuntu with systemd. Beyond three-network latency checks and alerts, it offers panel-triggered tests, per-VPS likes, comments and Markdown write-ups, one-click backup and migration, remote SWAP expansion, and theme samples you can hand to an AI to generate new themes. Aimed at people running their own VPS dashboards.

item.title: [juejin] 面试官问你：“AI 能写 80% 的代码了，公司为什么还需要你？”
item.description: A Juejin post on how 2026 technical interviews differ from two years ago: instead of hand-writing a Promise or explaining React Fiber, interviewers now assume candidates already use AI and ask why a company should still hire them when AI writes 80% of the code. It's aimed at engineers preparing for interviews who need to articulate what AI can't replace.

The roundup covers the Jakarta EE 12 schedule for each profile, Eclipse JNoSQL's promotion from incubation to an EE4J project, and JobRunr 9.0.0, which adds a Gantt-chart view of job lifecycles to its dashboard.

item.title: [infoq] Cloudflare 修复了容器中的跨租户数据泄露问题
item.description: Cloudflare disclosed and fixed a cross-tenant data leak in its Containers platform, which also backs Cloudflare Sandboxes. Container disks are thinly provisioned by dm-thin in 64 KiB blocks with zeroing skipped, so a 4 KiB write could leave roughly 60 KiB of a previous tenant's data readable. Researcher Oren Yomtov reported it on September 4; all 5,614 testable directory blocks across six production deployments came from other users. Cloudflare says it found no evidence of exploitation.

item.description: Chen Guangyu (Nathan Chen), a 17-year-old co-first author of the Attention Residuals paper who worked on scaling and pretraining for Kimi K3 at Moonshot AI, announced on October 15 that he has left the company and will move to the San Francisco Bay Area. Anthropic researcher Sholto Douglas invited him to work there, sparking speculation he would join Anthropic, which Chen flatly denied. His next employer and start date remain unknown.

item.title: [hackernews] Muse Spark Open
item.description: Meta released an open model called Muse Spark Open, with a Hugging Face repo at meta-models/Muse-Spark-Open-816B-A42B, a "Build with Muse Spark Open" post on dev.meta.ai and coverage from 9to5Mac. The 816B-A42B naming points to 816B total parameters with roughly 42B active, which matters to developers following large open-weight releases and sparse architectures.

item.title: [infoq] OpenCode 2.0 正式发布：一次“重大改造”，旧插件全部报废
item.description: OpenCode 2.0 is now stable: the open-source coding agent, with 214,000 GitHub stars, has moved to a Node.js/Electron architecture after three months of beta, a change its company Anomaly calls a major rework. Plugins written for 1.x no longer run and integrations built on the old server API must be updated; changelogs now track 2.x and updates no longer install silently, so users must upgrade manually.

item.title: [infoq] Gemini 4 Argon：为您解决最棘手的问题
item.description: Google launched Gemini 4 Argon, available now through the Gemini API as well as Antigravity, the Gemini App and AI Mode in Search, at $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens, with a 95% discount on cached input. Google says it beats other frontier models on multi-step tasks and tops the Vals index, and that internal teams used it to split out a roughly 6-million-line legacy Chrome code folder in weeks instead of months.

item.title: [hackernews] Solar surpasses nuclear power globally for first time
item.description: According to the WNISR 2026 report, solar generation surpassed nuclear power worldwide for the first time in 2025, and wind plus solar keep widening the gap. The report attributes this to nuclear's slow growth, long construction timelines and limited small modular reactor deployment, set against rapid renewables and battery expansion — relevant to anyone tracking energy mixes or power investment.

It ships desktop apps for macOS, Windows and Linux plus mobile and a remote runtime, under the MIT license. Useful for developers juggling several agents at once.

Its headline finding: 90% of US working hours go to tasks those benchmarks don't cover well. For anyone building agent evals or picking deployment targets, the gap between leaderboard scores and real productivity is the point.

The case points at how police surveillance systems are access-controlled, and at what happens when law-enforcement data access reaches into an officer's household.

The pay-per-success model targets teams building retrieval or browsing agents that need fresh pages rather than a static index. Beyond the APIs' purpose and price, coverage and rate limits aren't spelled out in the available material.

item.title: [github_trending] akitaonrails/ai-memory
item.description: ai-memory is an MIT-licensed Rust tool (Rust 1.95+) that gives coding agents such as Claude Code and OpenAI Codex a shared long-term memory, so you can quit one mid-task and pick up in another without re-explaining the architecture, the failed approaches or the open questions. It targets a common limit: built-in memory features live on one machine, belong to one agent, and vanish when you switch tools or hand off to a teammate.

item.title: [github_trending] headroomlabs-ai/headroom
item.description: Headroom is a context compression layer that shrinks tool output, logs, files and RAG chunks before they reach the LLM, available as a library, a proxy and an MCP server. The project reports roughly 20% fewer tokens for coding agents and 60-95% for JSON with unchanged answers; its demo compresses a 55,957-token prompt to 24,340 tokens while a critical FATAL line survives byte for byte. Aimed at agent developers paying per token or fighting context limits.
